Six functions call `get_default_renderer()` directly. I found them by searching `django/` for the name and finding the function that contains each call.

| File | Caller | How it's called |
|---|---|---|
| `django/template/autoreload.py` | `reset_loaders` | Imports it locally, then `getattr(get_default_renderer(), "engine", None)` |
| `django/forms/utils.py` | `ErrorDict.__init__` | `self.renderer = renderer or get_default_renderer()` |
| `django/forms/utils.py` | `ErrorList.__init__` | `self.renderer = renderer or get_default_renderer()` |
| `django/forms/forms.py` | `BaseForm.__init__` | `renderer = get_default_renderer()` |
| `django/forms/formsets.py` | `BaseFormSet.__init__` | `self.renderer = self.renderer or get_default_renderer()` |
| `django/forms/widgets.py` | `Widget._render` | `renderer = get_default_renderer()` |

I left out the two functions in `django/test/signals.py`. They only call `get_default_renderer.cache_clear()`, which clears its cache but never calls `get_default_renderer` itself. No other module imports it under a different name or re-exports it.
